notes: Verified: go vet clean; go test ./internal/tracking ./internal/webui ./internal/httpapi (tracking tests) pass; web vitest 134/134 pass; tsc -b clean; `vite build` reproduces the committed dist hash (index-CtJvru5t.js), so the embedded bundle matches the source.

Tests genuinely exercise the change: default-off byte-identical CSP + no DB row, nonce in header==nonce in snippet and rotating per request, proxy strips Cookie/Set-Cookie, disable restores base policy, invalid inputs ('unsafe-inline' in allowed_hosts, bare host, unknown provider, unknown field, >8KB snippet) rejected with 400, CSP report accumulate/allow/clear flow.

server/internal/tracking/tracking.go:288,382 withNonce/SnippetOrigins use byte offsets from strings.ToLower(remaining) against the original string. For characters whose lowercase form changes byte length (İ U+0130, Kelvin K U+212A, Ohm Ω U+2126) the offsets drift: reproduced locally with a custom snippet containing many 'İ' — the nonce attribute was written into the middle of a JS string and the <script tag was split into `<scr nonce=..ipt`, producing invalid UTF-8 and a non-executing snippet. Admin-only input and no security impact (the snippet is already admin-controlled), but a real corruption path; fix by lowering only for search via a case-insensitive scan or by using bytes.EqualFold-style matching.

server/internal/tracking/tracking.go:418 originOf (used for momento_url/matomo_url) accepts hosts containing ; ' " , (Go url.Parse allows them), unlike isPolicyOrigin for allowed_hosts. Checked: whitespace/control chars are rejected by url.Parse, so a new CSP directive or source cannot be injected (`;script-src'unsafe-inline'` is not a valid directive name; a `,` only adds a second, stricter policy). Not exploitable to loosen the policy, but the two validators should be aligned.

Risk to be aware of: /momento/* is an unauthenticated GET/POST relay to whatever momento_url a settings.write administrator configures (any path/query under that origin, with X-Forwarded-For). A settings.write user can thus point the Server at an internal host and let anonymous clients reach it through the console origin (SSRF-by-configuration). Same trust level as existing admin-configured outbound URLs; documented in ADMIN_GUIDE 20.3 but worth noting for deployments where settings.write is granted broadly. No rate limit on /momento/* or the csp-report endpoint (the recorder is bounded to 100 entries so memory is safe).
server/internal/httpapi/tracking.go:527 when the 256KB body cap is exceeded, ReverseProxy reports it through ErrorHandler as 502 'collector did not answer' rather than 413 — misleading but harmless.

server/internal/httpapi/server.go:730 every document-path request (including SPA 404 fallbacks and favicon-type misses) now does one server_metadata read; on DB failure it logs a warning per page request. Acceptable given existing handlers also use request ctx without a timeout, but could be noisy during an outage.
Behaviour change not called out: while tracking is active, img-src gains `data:` (previously covered by default-src 'self' only). Minor widening, only while tracking is on.

Reversibility: no schema migration; only a server_metadata row keyed tracking_policy is written when an admin saves. Reverting the code leaves the row ignored. Docs/PDF/README changes are all in scope.
